questions.question: Why is inline prose citation (e.g. 'According to page 12...') fragile in a multi-step pipeline?
options: It takes up too much storage space
Downstream steps like summarization, re-templating, or merging can silently drop or detach the citation since nothing structurally binds it to the claim
Prose citations are not supported by the Claude API at all
It's fragile only when the source is a PDF, not other formats

questions.question: What is the robust alternative to inline prose citation for preserving attribution?
options: A separate lookup database matched by claim ID
Structured claim-source pairs: each finding is its own record with the claim and source metadata (URL, document, page, date) in separate fields
Always quoting the source verbatim inside the claim text
Storing only the source URL and discarding the specific claim text

questions.question: Why does keeping source metadata in separate fields (rather than inline in the claim text) survive downstream transformation?
options: Because separate fields are automatically excluded from summarization
Because the source travels with the claim as structured data rather than as text that must be parsed back out
Because the Claude API automatically re-attaches citations to summaries
Because structured fields can't be edited by downstream code

questions.question: How does the structured claim-source pattern handle two sources that disagree on a value?
options: It always picks the more recent source and discards the other
It keeps both claim-source records intact so a downstream consumer can weigh recency or authority themselves
It averages the two conflicting values automatically
It flags the entire document as invalid

questions.question: How does this pattern relate to Claude's actual citations API feature?
options: They are unrelated — citations API is only for chat, not pipelines
The citations API already returns structured citation objects mapping generated text to source locations, which is the same design principle generalized
The citations API replaces the need for structured claim-source pairs entirely in every pipeline
Structured claim-source mapping was deprecated in favor of the citations API

questions.question: When is the overhead of structured claim-source pairs least likely to be worth it?
options: When the output feeds further synthesis or merging by other systems
For genuinely single-shot, human-read-once outputs that nothing downstream will reprocess
When there are multiple conflicting sources for the same claim
When the pipeline needs to catch semantic validation errors
